source_citation: Menna and Poulain (2014), Geostrophic currents and kinetic energies in the Black Sea estimated from merged drifter and satellite altimetry data, Ocean Science 10, 155-165, doi:10.5194/os-10-155-2014.
source_locator: Introduction; Section 2; Sections 3.1 and 3.2.1: surface geostrophic context, seasonal anomalies and Rim circuit around interior gyres.
source_license: Publisher PDF states CC Attribution 3.0. No source figures, trajectories or velocity grids packaged.
layer: Surface geostrophic circulation context; source drifters have mixed near-surface support through the first 15 m, with wind-driven components estimated separately. No uniform full-depth axis inferred.
sampling_context: 1999-2009 study with 89 drifters combined with altimetry; seasonal and interannual statistics.
topology_decision: Declared counterclockwise closed reference circuit, with arbitrary repeated anchor rather than current origin or termination. Not a continuously observed parcel circuit.
seasonal_continuity: Source describes stronger winter Rim flow and weaker/more fragmented summer-fall circulation. Closed reference geography does not establish continuity in every month.
excluded_objects: Coastal mesoscale eddies and their loops
Northern/southern Copernicus intensity monitoring windows treated as full-current endpoints
naming_overlap: Caucasus and Southern Current historical-name equivalence remains unresolved; no alias admission.
next_action: Review source-period convention, bathymetry and seasonal continuity before canonical admission; closed circuit candidate now available.
state_scope_note: The Black Sea has no dedicated state in this 56-state display inventory. Raw MEDI/REDS polygon contacts are coarse-shape artifacts, retained in the audit and excluded from state navigation; they do not place the circuit in the Mediterranean or Red Sea.
